headline: Rent growth and buybacks lift per-share results
summary_short: Revenue rose 2.8% y/y to $470.1M on higher rental rates, diluted EPS grew to $0.31 from $0.28 y/y, and Adjusted FFO grew 5.4% y/y to $186.0M even as Same-Home occupancy eased to 96.0% and turnover ticked up to 8.1%.
summary_long: Revenue grew 2.8% y/y to $470.1M on higher rental rates (Same-Home Average Monthly Realized Rent +2.6% to $2,346), partly offset by softer Same-Home occupancy (96.0% vs 96.4%) and higher turnover (8.1% vs 7.5%). Net income (common) rose 7.6% to $113.6M as revenue growth outpaced expenses and property-sale gains increased. FFO/Core FFO/AFFO all grew y/y ($194.0M/$202.8M/$186.0M). AMH repurchased $123.0M of stock in the quarter (all under the new 2026 program) and declared a $0.33/share dividend, up 10% y/y. Long-term debt was roughly flat y/y at $5,130.1M; equity fell 5.0% to $6,807.6M on the buybacks. Cash fell to $83.7M from $323.3M y/y on last year's note proceeds and this year's repurchases. No forward guidance disclosed in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Net income grew as rents and other single-family property revenues outpaced total expense growth, with higher net gains on property sales, partially offset by lower other income.
Revenue growth was primarily driven by higher rental rates.

Same drivers as diluted EPS: net income growth plus a lower weighted average share count from repurchases.
Increases in rents and other single-family property revenues exceeded increases in total expenses, plus higher net gains on property sales, partially offset by lower other income and expense, net.
Not separately explained in the release; mirrors net income growth plus the standard NAREIT real-estate D&A add-back.
Not separately explained in the release; FFO growth plus modestly higher one-time addback items (transaction costs, share-based comp) versus the prior year.
Core FFO growth plus lower Recurring Capital Expenditures ($15.9M vs $20.5M y/y) and lower leasing costs, per the company's own AFFO reconciliation.
Y/y decline reflects 2025's one-time unsecured senior notes issuance and this year's share repurchases, per the financing-activities discussion.
Roughly unchanged y/y: no new senior notes were issued in 2026, offset by a higher revolving-credit-facility balance.
Decline is consistent with $238.2M of six-month share repurchases exceeding retained net income; not explicitly framed as an equity driver in the release.
